column2: Her favorite aphorism, "Well begun is half done," hung in a frame above her desk.
column3: 她最愛的格言「好的開始是成功的一半」裱框掛在書桌上方。
column5: 諧音「阿佛瑞森」：阿佛每天一句短短的人生智慧

column2: Her scout leader's maxim, "leave the campsite cleaner than you found it," guided every trip.
column3: 童軍領隊的座右銘「離開時讓營地比來時更乾淨」，指引著每一趟旅行。
column4: live by a maxim (奉行座右銘)
column5: max 最大：人生最大的規則，濃縮成一句話

column2: The old adage "a stitch in time saves nine" reminded him to fix the leak at once.
column3: 古諺「及時一針省九針」提醒他立刻修好漏水處。
column5: 諧音「愛地句」：老人家最愛掛在嘴邊的老話

column2: The graduation speech offered only platitudes like "follow your dreams," and nothing students could actually use.
column3: 畢業演講只有「追隨夢想」之類的老生常談，沒有任何學生真正用得上的內容。
column5: plat 像 flat 平：平淡無奇、沒有深度的話

column2: Calling the villain "pure evil" felt like a cliche, so the editor asked for a fresher description.
column3: 把反派稱作「純粹的邪惡」顯得老套，編輯要求更新鮮的描寫。
column4: a tired cliche (老掉牙的套語)
column5: 諧音「克立些」：每個人都說過的話，聽了想睡覺

column2: It is a truism that practice improves skill, yet few people practice consistently.
column3: 練習能增進技能是人人皆知的道理，但很少人能持續練習。
column4: a simple truism (淺顯的老道理)
column5: tru(e) 真 + ism：真得不能再真，說了等於白說

column2: In geometry, the axiom that a straight line joins any two points needs no proof.
column3: 在幾何學中，兩點之間可連成一條直線這條公理，不需要證明。
column5: 諧音「俺可信」：我不用證明就可以相信

column2: Einstein postulated that the speed of light is constant for every observer.
column3: 愛因斯坦假定光速對每位觀察者而言都是定值。
column5: post 貼出：把前提先貼在牆上，當作不必證明的起點

column2: Saying "the rule is the rule" is a tautology that explains nothing.
column3: 說「規定就是規定」是一種什麼也沒解釋的同義反覆。
column4: a logical tautology (邏輯上的套套)
column5: tauto 相同 + logy 說法：同一句話換個方式說兩次

column2: Free gift and "added bonus" are pleonasms that waste words without adding any meaning.
column3: 「免費贈品」和「額外紅利」這類累贅表達浪費字詞，卻沒增添任何意思。
column5: pleo 更多：話說得比需要的還多，字數太多了

column2: Extreme solipsism holds that only one's own mind is certain to exist, so other people may be illusions.
column3: 極端的唯我論主張只有自己的心靈確定存在，其他人可能只是幻象。
column5: sol 單獨 + ips 自己：世界上只有我自己存在

column2: Disillusioned by war, the poet drifted into nihilism, doubting that life holds any purpose or value.
column3: 戰爭使詩人幻滅，他陷入虛無主義，懷疑人生有任何目的或價值。
column5: nihil 是拉丁文「無」，annihilate 也有它：什麼都沒有

column2: Her fatalism led her to shrug at warnings, insisting that whatever was destined would happen anyway.
column3: 她的宿命論讓她對警告聳聳肩，堅稱注定的事終究會發生。
column5: fate 命運 + alism：相信命運早已寫好，只能接受

column2: Strict determinism claims every event, including human choice, follows necessarily from earlier causes.
column3: 嚴格的決定論主張所有事件，包括人的選擇，都必然源自先前的原因。
column5: determine 決定 + ism：一切都被前因決定，像排好的骨牌

column2: Cultural relativism urges us to judge customs by their own society's standards, not our own.
column3: 文化相對主義主張，要以各社會自己的標準，而非我們的標準來評斷習俗。
column5: relative 相對的：真理看你站在哪個角度

column2: Empiricism holds that knowledge comes from observation and experiment rather than pure reasoning.
column3: 經驗主義主張知識來自觀察與實驗，而不是純粹的推理。
column5: em 在內 + peir 試驗，和 experiment 同家族：親身試過才算數

column2: Descartes' rationalism trusted logical thought over the senses as the path to certain knowledge.
column3: 笛卡兒的理性主義相信，邏輯思考比感官更能通往確定的知識。
column5: rational 理性 + ism：相信腦袋推理比眼睛看更可靠

column2: His pragmatism showed in meetings: he ignored grand theories and asked only what would actually work.
column3: 他的實用主義表現在會議上：他不理會宏大的理論，只問什麼真正行得通。
column5: pragma 是「行動」，和 practical 同家族：有用才算數

column2: Her friends called the resort weekend pure hedonism, devoted to pleasure and nothing else.
column3: 朋友說那個度假村週末純粹是享樂主義，只為了追求快樂。
column5: hed 像 head：腦袋裡只想著吃喝玩樂的快樂
